legalCutoffPolicy: Verify applicable consolidated texts, amendments, corrigenda, RTS/ITS and authority requirements at each run source cutoff.
applicabilityPolicy: Record assessed entity role, size, exemptions, standard/simplified regime, critical-function scope, TLPT selection and critical-provider designation. Non-applicability is scoped out explicitly; it is never an automatic pass, failure or fabricated score.

areas.title: DORA: Applicability, proportionality and governance
areas.summary: Identify the assessed legal entity, its DORA role, applicable regime and management-body accountability.
areas.boundaries: Determine financial-entity category, exemptions, group boundary, size and proportionality; distinguish the standard and simplified ICT frameworks and the role of non-critical versus designated critical ICT providers. Cover management-body ownership, resourcing and ICT-risk oversight. Do not treat every provider as directly subject to every financial-entity obligation.
areas.keywords: entity scope, proportionality, management body, simplified framework, applicability, governance

areas.title: DORA: ICT risk framework and assurance
areas.summary: Maintain a documented, approved ICT risk framework and resilience strategy with accountable review and assurance.
areas.boundaries: Cover the framework, risk tolerance, strategy, independent control/assurance functions, audit follow-up and framework reviews. SFS 0 owns entity applicability and board accountability; SFS A owns staff learning and information sharing.
areas.keywords: ICT risk management framework, risk tolerance, digital operational resilience strategy, internal audit, assurance

areas.title: DORA: ICT assets, services and dependency mapping
areas.summary: Identify critical functions and the assets, information and dependencies that support them.
areas.boundaries: Cover business-function classification, inventories, ownership, dependency maps, ICT adequacy and legacy-system risk assessment. SFS D owns third-party arrangements and the regulatory register; SFS 4 owns changes and vulnerabilities.
areas.keywords: critical or important functions, asset inventory, dependency mapping, information assets, legacy systems

areas.title: DORA: Protection, access and data security
areas.summary: Protect ICT systems and information through proportionate access, data and network safeguards.
areas.boundaries: Cover identity and access controls, authentication, least privilege, cryptography, data security, physical/environmental safeguards and network segregation. Apply the relevant standard or simplified framework. SFS 4 owns change/patch lifecycle; SFS 5 owns detection.
areas.keywords: identity and access management, authentication, encryption, network security, data protection, physical security

areas.title: DORA: Secure change, development and vulnerability management
areas.summary: Control ICT changes, software/system development, vulnerabilities and patching.
areas.boundaries: Cover acquisition and development controls, testing before deployment, change approval, emergency changes, patching, vulnerability treatment and supported-system lifecycle. Use the applicable ICT-risk technical standards; do not substitute a generic development maturity score.
areas.keywords: ICT change management, secure development, vulnerability management, patch management, ICT lifecycle

areas.title: DORA: Monitoring and anomalous activity detection
areas.summary: Detect anomalous activity, performance issues and ICT-related incidents using monitored evidence.
areas.boundaries: Cover detection thresholds, logging, alerting, monitoring responsibilities, escalation triggers and testing of detection capability. SFS 6 owns handling/classification after detection; SFS 7 owns external reporting.
areas.keywords: monitoring, detection mechanisms, alert thresholds, logging, anomalous activity, ICT incidents

areas.title: DORA: Incident management and classification
areas.summary: Record, handle and classify ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats using an accountable process.
areas.boundaries: Cover incident handling workflows, ownership, tracking, prioritisation, root cause and classification criteria. Distinguish ordinary incidents, major ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats. SFS 7 owns reporting deadlines, forms and recipients.
areas.keywords: ICT incident management, incident classification, major incidents, significant cyber threats, root cause

areas.title: DORA: Incident reporting and communications
areas.summary: Notify and report applicable incidents using current competent-authority requirements and communication plans.
areas.boundaries: Cover initial/intermediate/final reports, voluntary significant-threat notifications, delegated reporting responsibilities, client/stakeholder communication and applicable operational/payment-security incidents. Verify current RTS/ITS timing and templates from sources; do not invent deadlines or assume one authority for every entity.
areas.keywords: incident reporting, competent authority, notification, reporting templates, crisis communications, payment incidents

areas.title: DORA: ICT business continuity and crisis response
areas.summary: Maintain and test continuity and response arrangements for critical functions and disruptive scenarios.
areas.boundaries: Cover business impact analysis, continuity policy, response/recovery plans, crisis management, activation, dependencies and continuity exercises. SFS 9 owns backup/restore controls; SFS B owns the wider resilience test programme.
areas.keywords: ICT business continuity, business impact analysis, crisis management, response plans, continuity exercises

areas.title: DORA: Backup, restoration and recovery
areas.summary: Protect backup copies and demonstrate restoration and recovery against stated objectives.
areas.boundaries: Cover backup scope, segregation and protection, restoration testing, recovery priorities/objectives, redundant capacity and reconciliation of recovered information. Keep business continuity policy in SFS 8 and evidence of real execution separate from proposed procedures.
areas.keywords: backup policies, restoration, recovery time, recovery point, redundant capacity, data reconciliation

areas.title: DORA: Learning, staff readiness and information sharing
areas.summary: Use incident/test lessons, staff readiness and controlled information sharing to improve resilience.
areas.boundaries: Cover post-incident learning, training and awareness for staff and management, relevant provider participation, intelligence sharing arrangements and applicable authority notifications. Sharing participation is conditional; non-participation is not automatically a statutory failure. SFS 1 owns framework assurance.
areas.keywords: lessons learned, staff training, security awareness, threat intelligence sharing, information sharing arrangements

areas.title: DORA: Digital operational resilience testing programme
areas.summary: Maintain a risk-based testing programme, findings register and verified remediation.
areas.boundaries: Cover test planning, independence, relevant systems/functions, suitable test types, remediation and closure evidence. Distinguish ordinary testing requirements from the conditional advanced TLPT regime in SFS C.
areas.keywords: resilience testing programme, testing independence, test coverage, remediation, findings closure

areas.title: DORA: Threat-led penetration testing
areas.summary: Determine TLPT applicability and govern advanced testing where the entity is selected or required to participate.
areas.boundaries: Cover authority-driven selection, test scope, critical functions, tester independence/qualification, threat intelligence, live-system safeguards, third-party participation, remediation and mutual recognition. Do not impose TLPT on all financial entities or claim tests were executed by generating a plan.
areas.keywords: TLPT applicability, threat-led penetration testing, tester requirements, critical functions, testing safeguards

areas.title: DORA: ICT third-party risk, concentration and register
areas.summary: Govern ICT provider arrangements, due diligence, concentration risk and the register of information.
areas.boundaries: Cover third-party strategy, accountable ownership, pre-contract assessment, provider selection, conflicts, concentration and the entity/group register with applicable submissions. SFS E owns contractual clauses, subcontracting and exits; SFS F owns designated-provider oversight interactions.
areas.keywords: ICT third-party risk, due diligence, concentration risk, register of information, contractual arrangements

areas.title: DORA: Provider contracts, subcontracting and exit
areas.summary: Maintain enforceable ICT contract controls, subcontracting oversight and tested exit arrangements.
areas.boundaries: Cover contractual rights and obligations, service levels, locations/data access, audit/inspection rights, incident assistance, subcontracting changes and termination/exit strategies. Distinguish additional requirements for critical or important functions from baseline contract requirements.
areas.keywords: ICT contracts, service levels, subcontracting, audit rights, termination rights, exit strategy

areas.title: DORA: Critical provider oversight and supervisory readiness
areas.summary: Prepare the assessed entity for applicable critical-provider oversight and supervisory cooperation.
areas.boundaries: Distinguish financial-entity duties from duties of designated critical ICT providers and powers of ESAs/competent authorities. Cover designation implications, supervisory requests, access/inspection cooperation, oversight findings, remediation and records. Never score an authority power as an operational duty of an ordinary provider or financial entity.
areas.keywords: critical ICT provider designation, ESA oversight, lead overseer, supervisory cooperation, inspections, remediation
